note_sections.t: Persistent elevation of prostate-specific antigen combined with prior histological confirmation of low-grade malignancy necessitates clinical reassessment.

Mr. X is a 58-year-old retired mechanical engineer who lives in a multi-generational home with his spouse and adult daughter. A non-smoker, he maintains an alcohol-free lifestyle and performs chair-based exercises to accommodate limited mobility. Urinary complaints are minimal, scoring 2 out of 35 on the IPSS. His medical background includes hypertension, currently managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, and metoprolol. Additional historical points feature a stable HbA1c of 6.4%, a remote appendectomy during his thirties, and a recent vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins, with no accompanying systemic complaints or bone pain.

DRE: The prostate exhibits a symmetric enlargement characterized by a smooth, firm consistency. Palpation identifies no nodules or asymmetrical areas. General survey shows stable vital signs, an unremarkable abdominal exam, and no palpable lymphadenopathy.
